title: Replication and Partitioning
focus: Specify fresh, bounded-stale, read-your-writes, monotonic, causal, and linearizable requirements per operation.

pacing.review: Skim lessons, answer self-checks, and take one generated quiz.
pacing.standard: Study lessons, complete guided practice, use the answer key, and take one or more generated quizzes.
pacing.deep: Complete standard work plus the reinforcement lab and optional project.

lessons.title: Hot Keys, Skew, Fairness, and Tenant Isolation
CAP, PACELC, Regional Placement, Security, and Cost

learning_outcomes.statement: Specify fresh, bounded-stale, read-your-writes, monotonic, causal, and linearizable requirements per operation.
Compare leader/follower, multi-leader, and leaderless replication with explicit synchronous and asynchronous acknowledgement boundaries.
Calculate quorum intersections and diagnose failures in membership, durability, concurrent-version, and sloppy-quorum assumptions.
Implement selectable version metadata, conflict preservation, read repair, and anti-entropy with convergence evidence.
Compare hash, range, and consistent-hash partitioning using balance, movement, routing, and safe reshard evidence.
Diagnose replica partition, leader loss, lag, lost acknowledgement, hot key, and reshard failures from immutable same-input evidence.
Design tenant isolation, regional placement, residency controls, capacity, repair ownership, migration, rollback, and cost.
Synthesize the module mechanisms across earlier topics and explain the decision tradeoffs from evidence.

lab.note: Use the lab to reinforce the local mechanism; treat expanded matrices and platform-specific evidence as optional deep-dive work.

optional_project.description: Apply Replication and Partitioning to a small system you know. Write a short design note, experiment report, or implementation summary only if you want deeper practice.
